https://www.mirror.co.uk/news/uk-news/re.text:
Rat-sized spiders are set to invade the UK, and Brits are being given advice on how to keep them out of their homes.
The fen raft spider, capable of hunting and killing fish, was once close to extinction but is now making a comeback thanks to careful cultivation of the country's wetlands by the Royal Society for the Protection of Birds (RSPB). Despite this being good news for the wetlands ecology, it's not so great for the half of Brits who admit to having arachnophobia.
To keep these eight-legged creatures at bay, Sam Jenkinson, a garden building expert at Tiger, suggests using natural repellents such as peppermint, citrus, and vinegar, which spiders dislike. A homemade peppermint spray can be made by mixing 10-15 drops of peppermint essential oil with water in a spray bottle and spraying around your home, especially near windowsills, doorways, and other potential entry points.
Citrus peels or cotton balls dipped in vinegar can also be placed around your home for a similar effect. Another effective method is to seal any cracks and entry points in your home, reports Lancs Live. And Spiders can sneak in through the tiniest of gaps, so it's crucial to seal them up. Pay extra attention to windows, doors, and vents. Use caulk or sealant to close any cracks or gaps where necessary.
Spiders are drawn to clutter and debris, so keeping your home and garden buildings neat and tidy is key. Regular vacuuming, dusting, and decluttering are essential.
Certain plants like peppermint, lavender, basil, and citronella are known to repel spiders. Plant these around your garden to keep spiders away from both your garden buildings and your home.
Spiders are insectivores, so eliminating insect pests in your home is important. You can use traps, baits, or insecticides to deal with insects.
Spiders find firewood attractive for various reasons - they can use it as shelter, build webs, and lay eggs in it. Firewood also attracts other insects which serve as food for spiders. Store your firewood in a place where you'd prefer not to encounter a creepy crawly.
